summary: For each successful call of estimate_pose_chamfer_v3_2, write the pallet width, height, and depth in metres on the stage-2 outcome and on PalletPoseStamped after deferred_source_indices. Width is params.pallet_width_m and height is params.pallet_height_m, the prototype sizes cached_prototype already passes to build_default_pallet_prototype for that call. The search template stays that face. Depth is the face-centre range this call already stores as pose.tz: lift_point_from_plane_2d and apply_se3 produce centre_r, and centre_r.z() is the z of that centre in the camera RGB optical frame. publish_pose already copies that scalar into pose.position.z. The same scalar is depth_m. Those three scalars and has_dimensions are set on the outcome before return. has_dimensions is true on that success. publish_pose copies has_dimensions, width_m, height_m, and depth_m onto the rich message. The face-centre position and yaw stay the pose. The admitted source index and the deferred source indices stay the lists published_admission_split already writes. The rich message already carries this pair's RGB and depth stamps, so the three sizes belong to this capture while the scene can still change. A failed estimate leaves has_dimensions false, publishes no PalletPoseStamped, and the failure diagnostic stays the admission lists it already carries. The two early returns in on_pair stay silent. Stage 2 still runs once, on the one candidate the pose node admits. The geometry_msgs pose stays a header and a pose. The user named the three sizes. The part they did not name is that width and height are the prototype face this match already uses, and depth is that estimated optical-frame z, written with those sizes on the pose result the handling process reads.
hypothesis: PalletPoseStamped already carries this capture's face centre and admission split, while the prototype width, the prototype height, and the estimated face range stay off the size fields. Copying that face and that optical-frame z onto the pose result gives the handling process the pallet width, height, and depth for the pallet this synchronized capture is about to handle.
